para.text: HOW TO USE THE RULER OPTION

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;

para.text: The ruler option produces a horizontal and a vertical hairline in the graph to measure the co-ordinates of lines, points etc. The ruler option is available in all 2D plots,
and in 3D plots that use 2D procedures. The latter are: the contour plot, and the dead-point side and top views.
Note that the functions of the ruler are affected by data tracking (see

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;

text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: The ruler option uses the mouse, but XYGRAPH is not capable of automatically generating mouse event handlers, so you must create mouse event handlers yourself and copy these with the procedures
(see the description of these procedures for detailed explanation).

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;

para.text: The use of the ruler option is simple: just click with the mouse in the
(left-click). In default conditions the colour of the hairlines is the foreground colour defined in

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: the ruler also follows polar co-ordinates.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;

text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: Note that it is possible that with a very unfortunate combination of foreground colour and background colour the hairlines are not visible (notably when both are grey).

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;

text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: you can set the colour of the hairlines and the position of the display of the co-ordinates, and the appearance of the ruler lines. If your graph has multiple Y-axes you can switch between the Y-axes by clicking the right mouse button. The colour in the display indicates the related Y-axis.
This procedure can also be used in 3D mode, but the 3D equivalent
will enable extra options in contour plotting.

para.text: An option is to use the ruler in relative mode, that means that not the absolute co-ordinates are given but the co-ordinates relative to some position on the screen. To switch relative mode on and off simply click the middle mouse button (assuming this has been installed properly on your computer), or hit the spacebar. The latter works only after the key events are copied with
, but the action is sometimes intercepted by Windows to perform other actions. The relative mode is convenient for measuring dimensions on the screen. Relative mode can be disabled, see
Relative mode is not available in data tracking

para.text: enables simple data tracking, see that procedure's description. However this also enables another ruler mode that is not present in 'normal' operations: tracking with the cursor keys.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: If data tracking is enabled, and you release the mouse button with the Shift-key pressed (or simply Shift-click the mouse), the ruler is not switched off but stays present. You can now move the ruler with the cursor keys, or better: let the ruler snap to the next data point. As a reminder the cursor stays a handpointer instead of the normal arrow.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: Te keys cursor-left and cursor-right (also on the num keypad at the right hand side of the keyboard) move the ruler in X-direction, and the keys cursor-up and cursor-down select another column of Y-data (if present and enabled). Note that the latter does not necessarily imply that the ruler actually moves upwards or downwards respectively.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: This mode can be switched off by pressing the Enter key, or by any mouse click.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: If the graph is zoomed some data points may fall outside the visible area, these cannot be tracked. However if you keep the Ctrl key pressed while hitting the cursor keys the graph will scroll if necessary so that the requested data point will always be inside the visible area.
